chunks: Ahmad ibn al-Hasan al-Qattan narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Sa'id al-Hamadani narrated to us, saying: Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Fadhal narrated to us, from his father, from Marwan ibn Muslim, from Thabit ibn Abi Safiyyah, from Sa'd al-Khaffaf, from al-Asbagh ibn Nubata, who said: The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said:

The wise men in the past said: One should go to the doors for ten reasons. First, the House of God, Exalted and Mighty, to perform its pilgrimage rites, fulfill its right, and discharge its obligation. Second, the doors of kings, whose obedience is connected to the obedience of God, Exalted and Mighty; their right is obligatory, their benefit is great, and their harm is severe. Third, the doors of scholars, from whom religious and worldly knowledge is acquired. Fourth, the doors of the generous and giving people, who spend their wealth seeking praise and hoping for the Hereafter. Fifth, the doors of the foolish, who are needed in incidents and sought for in times of need. Sixth, the doors of those from whom one seeks to draw near, for the sake of seeking gifts, chivalry, and need. Seventh, the doors of those from whom benefit is expected in opinion and consultation, strengthening resolve, and receiving gifts for what is needed. Eighth, the doors of brothers, for the sake of maintaining ties and fulfilling their rights. Ninth, the doors of enemies, whose mischief is pacified by forbearance, and their evils are repelled by stratagems, gentleness, kindness, and visiting them. Tenth, the doors of those from whom one benefits by their company, from whom good manners are acquired, and who provide comfort in conversation.
ai.seo_question: What are the ten reasons for visiting doors according to Imam Ali in al-Khisal?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Khisal*, Imam Ali (peace be upon him) outlines a pragmatic framework for social interaction, categorizing visits to ten types of 'doors' based on their utility in fulfilling religious, intellectual, and worldly needs. This classification reflects the Shia emphasis on balancing spiritual devotion with practical engagement in society, highlighting the importance of maintaining ties with kings, scholars, and even enemies through diplomacy and good manners.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 10-3 Ahmad ibn al-Hassan al-Qat’tan narrated that Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Sa’id al-Hamedany quoted Ali ibn al-Hassan ibn Faz’zal, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Marvan ibn Muslim, on the authority of Sabit ibn Abi Safiyeh, on the authority of Sa’ed al-Khifaf, on the authority of Al-Asbaq ibn Nobatat that the Commander of the Faithful Imam Ali (MGB) said,

“The wise men in the past said that going to and coming from doors of houses should be for one of ten reasons.1- To go to the door of the House of the Honorable the Exalted God to perform the Hajj pilgrimage; fulfill His right and do what He has made obligatory upon you.2- To go to the doors of the just kings obeying whom is an extension of obeying the Honorable the Exalted God. Their right is an obligatory right; their benefit may be great; and their loss may also be great.3- To go to the doors of the houses of wise men who can be used to gain religious knowledge.4- To go to the doors of the houses of the generous people who grant their possessions to gain a good reputation and hope to get rewarded in the Hereafter.5- To go to the doors of the houses of the unwise people whom you may need at times of disaster or seek refuge to when you need it.6- To go to the doors of the houses of the noble men to ask them for gifts, chivalry or the fulfillment of your needs.7- To go to the doors of the houses of those whose opinion is asked and are consulted with to reinforce alertness and request grants to fulfill needs.8- To go to the doors of the houses of religious brothers to associate with and visit the relations of kin to fulfill their rights.9- To go to the doors of the houses of the enemies whose wickedness will be fended off by treating them with patience, wisdom and kindness.10- To go to the doors of the houses of those from whose association and good manners we can benefit.”
